passages.provision_quote: (a) Notwithstanding Section 30510, “assault weapon” also means any of the following: (1) A semiautomatic, centerfire rifle that does not have a fixed magazine but has any one of the following: (A) A pistol grip that protrudes conspicuously beneath the action of the weapon.
passages.note: Chaptered single-subject bill ("Firearms: assault weapons") whose operative sections widen the banned class of semiautomatic assault-style weapons and set registration for those already owned, leaving other firearms untouched.

rows.reasoning: McGuire voted Aye on final passage of SB 880 (2015-2016), a single-subject assault-weapons bill whose operative section redefines “assault weapon” to include “A semiautomatic, centerfire rifle that does not have a fixed magazine but has any one of the following: (A) A pistol grip that protrudes conspicuously beneath the action of the weapon.” That extends the prohibited class of semi-automatic assault-style weapons while other firearms, and Olympic-sanctioned competition pistols, remain lawful, which is the rung that would “Ban semi-automatic assault-style weapons, while allowing other firearms.” It excludes the rung banning civilian firearm ownership outright and the rungs that add no new restrictions or repeal major gun restrictions.
